Here’s a concise but thorough summary of what I know about the TV series Cleaners, plus pointers for finding more detail.

Basic overview
- Cleaners is an action/crime web/series that was produced for the Crackle streaming service.
- Premise: two young women who work as "cleaners" (fixers/hitwomen) for a shadowy organization take on assignments that involve cleaning up crime scenes, assassinations and other deniable work. As with many series in this genre, their assignments draw them into larger conspiracies and dangerous conflicts.
- Tone/genre: action, crime, thriller with dark humor and stylistic action sequences.

Principal cast and characters (major roles commonly associated with the show)
- Emmanuelle Chriqui — one of the two leads (a seasoned cleaner).
- Emily Osment — the other lead (younger partner/cleaner).
(They are the central duo the series follows.)

Production and release
- The show was produced and released on Crackle.
- It premiered in 2013. The show ran for multiple short-season web-series episodes (Crackle-style seasons); there was at least a second season following the initial run.
- Episodes were short-form/streaming length typical of Crackle originals (roughly 20–30 minutes each, rather than standard network hour-long episodes).

Recurring themes and elements
- Action-oriented set pieces, fight choreography and gunplay centered around the two leads.
- The narrative mixes episodic assignments (single jobs) with serialized story arcs about the organization that employs them and the fallout from their jobs.
- Character-driven tension between the two leads (personality differences and moral questions about their line of work).
- Conspiracy and corruption — local law enforcement, criminal factions and shadowy handlers play roles in the longer arcs.

Critical reception and audience
- The show had a niche audience: praised by some for the leads’ chemistry and action sequences; seen by others as pulpy and episodic. As a Crackle original it didn’t get the mainstream exposure of major-cable/streaming shows but found viewers who liked female-led action series.

Availability
- Originally available on Crackle. Availability may change over time — check Crackle, other streaming services, or digital purchase platforms if you want to watch now.

Limitations / caveat
- I’ve summarized the key, reliably-known points (premise, leads, platform, release window, tone). I don’t have a fully detailed episode-by-episode breakdown, an exact episode count per season, or a complete guest cast list at hand here; different sources sometimes list slightly different guest/recurring credits.
